classification.difficultyReason: Recognise two prominent peaks, the direction of each long tail and mirrored bar heights in four supplied histograms using the taught distribution vocabulary.

spec.description: Ten touching equal-width bars, retaining the two separated prominent peaks and the intervening low bars. No numerical axes, ticks or labels are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied question figure; no answer labels.

answer.worked: There are two separated prominent peaks, so the distribution is bimodal.

spec.description: Ten touching equal-width bars. The tallest bars are near the right, with a long low tail to the left. No numerical axes, ticks or labels are supplied.
spec.mathematics: Most observations are towards the right; the tail extends left.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied question figure; no answer labels.

answer.worked: Most of the data are concentrated towards the right, with a long tail to the left. The distribution is negatively skewed.

spec.description: Ten touching equal-width bars. The tallest bars are near the left, with a long low tail extending right. No numerical axes, ticks or labels are supplied.
spec.mathematics: Most observations are towards the left; the tail extends right.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied question figure; no answer labels.

answer.worked: Most of the data are concentrated towards the left, with a long tail to the right. The distribution is positively skewed.

spec.description: Ten touching equal-width bars with equal mirrored bar heights, two equal tallest central bars and matching outer shoulders. No numerical axes, ticks or labels are supplied.
spec.mathematics: Bar heights mirror one another about the centre.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied question figure; no answer labels.

answer.worked: The bar heights on the left mirror those on the right, so the distribution is symmetrical.
